title: "Arch Linux and the Rolling Model"
---

# Arch Linux and the Rolling Model

Arch Linux represents the purest embodiment of the **rolling release model**. There are no release freezes, no versioned upgrade cycles, and no point releases. Instead, the distribution operates as a living, continuous stream of updates.

```
+-----------------------------------------------------------+
|                   Arch Linux Release Pipeline             |
|                                                           |
| 1. Upstream Release Tag (e.g. Linux Kernel 6.10)          |
|         |                                                 |
|         v                                                 |
| 2. Arch Package Maintainer updates PKGBUILD               |
|         |                                                 |
|         v                                                 |
| 3. Uploaded to [core-testing] or [extra-testing]          |
|    - Maintainers and community test on physical hardware  |
|         |                                                 |
|         v (After validation / signs-off)                  |
| 4. Promoted to [core] or [extra] Repositories             |
|    - Synchronized instantly to global mirrors             |
|         |                                                 |
|         v                                                 |
| 5. End User executes `pacman -Syu`                        |
+-----------------------------------------------------------+
```

## Soname Bumps & Rebuild Traversal

In a rolling release, when a fundamental shared library updates its Application Binary Interface (ABI)—such as `libpng` bumping from `libpng16.so.16` to `libpng17.so.17`—all dependent packages will break immediately if executed against the old library.

Arch solves this through **rebuild lists**:
1. When `libpng` is updated, the maintainer queries the package database for all reverse dependencies:
   ```bash
   $ pactree -r libpng
   ```
2. The entire tree of affected packages (`feh`, `gimp`, `imagemagick`) is rebuilt simultaneously in `testing` against the new library.
3. The new library and all rebuilt packages are moved into the production `[core]` and `[extra]` repositories in a single atomic transaction.

## The Arch User Repository (AUR)

One of Arch's greatest innovations is the **Arch User Repository (AUR)**:
- A community-driven git repository containing millions of `PKGBUILD` source build recipes.
- Users compile software directly on their machines rather than relying on pre-compiled binaries from the distribution maintainers.
- Provides a bridge for esoteric, proprietary, or bleeding-edge software without burdening the official build infrastructure.
